question: On a branching FSM with session-dependent transitions (H(S_next|URL,H_K=3) > 0.2 bits), does non-trivial response encoding — realistic page-content structure (title, items, status) that varies with state but contains NO explicit state_id, session_token, direction, or step fields — yield conditional PMI I(S_next; Response_before | URL, H_K=3) > 0.05 bits with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.0125, thereby addressing the V10 identifiability concern that the parent's PMI was trivially constructed from explicit state label injection?
hypothesis: Page-content structure that varies with FSM state (but is not a state label) carries conditional predictive information about the next state when action-history is insufficient (H > 0.2 bits). The parent's BC PMI = 0.369 bits at K=3 may be entirely explained by explicit state_id/session_token/direction leakage (audit V10). If PMI persists with non-trivial encoding (page title, item list, status text), this demonstrates that realistic web-content variation — not just state label injection — carries predictive information about state transitions. If PMI drops to zero, the parent's signal was trivially constructed.
falsifier: The claim is falsified if ANY of: (1) conditional PMI I(S_next; Response_before | URL, H_K=3) <= 0.05 bits with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p >= 0.0125 on the non-trivial encoding condition; OR (2) positive control fails (|session-randomized BC PMI| >= 3 * std(permuted PMI) OR perm_null_std == 0 after excluding H=0 strata); OR (3) determinism check fails (P(Response_hash | FSM_state, session, step) < 1.0 on non-trivial encoding); OR (4) ceiling not eliminated (H(S_next|URL, H_K=3) <= 0.2 bits); OR (5) data quality insufficient (< 500 valid transitions); OR (6) cardinality degenerate (|R| >= 0.8 * N per stratum).
baselines: Trivial encoding baseline: same FSM, same sessions, but response contains explicit state_id, session_token, direction, step fields (parent's state-dependent response). Expected BC PMI > 0. Provides within-experiment comparison: identical FSM and sessions, only response encoding strategy differs. Directly tests V10: does removing explicit labels eliminate PMI?
State-independent baseline: same FSM, same sessions, but response is constant ('{"ok":true}') regardless of state. Expected BC PMI = 0. Provides estimator validation.
Action-history-only prediction P(S_next | URL, H_K) for K=1,2,3. On branching FSM, H(S_next|URL,H_K=3) > 0.2 bits, so action-history is insufficient.
Frequency baseline P(S_next) — marginal next-state distribution. Expected accuracy ~33%.
positive_control: Session-randomized control on non-trivial encoding: replace each trajectory's session_id with a random session_id from a different trajectory. Response content still varies (same generation), but session→state mapping is broken. Expected BC PMI ≈ 0. CRITICAL FIX from parent V2: exclude strata where H(S_next|stratum)=0 from min_perm_null_std computation. Pass criterion: |session-randomized BC PMI| < 3 * std(permuted PMI) AND perm_null_std > 0 (computed only on H>0 strata).
null_control: Shuffled response labels within (URL, ActionHistory_K, step) strata on non-trivial encoding: permute Response_before labels within each stratum, preserving marginal distributions. Expected BC PMI ≈ 0. Pass criterion: |mean shuffled BC PMI| < 3 * std(shuffled BC PMI). Compute bias-corrected shuffled PMI (shuffled - perm_mean) to remove finite-sample bias.
measurement_validity: Two conditions: non-trivial encoding (page title, items, status — no state labels) and trivial encoding (explicit state_id, session_token, direction, step). Same FSM, same sessions, same session assignment, only response content differs.
Session assignment identical across conditions: generate session_directions once, use identically for both conditions (fixes parent V7 session mismatch).
Each condition yields >= 500 valid transitions after filtering. 200 trajectories x 10 steps = 2000 total transitions per condition.
Bias-corrected MI estimator: observed PMI - permutation null mean (within-strata permutation, 1000 permutations per stratum).

Permutation test: 1000 permutations per (condition, K) stratum, shuffling Response_before labels within (URL, ActionHistory_K, step) strata. Bonferroni correction across 4 comparisons (2 conditions x 2 K values).
No target leakage: action history constructed from trajectory step ordering with START padding.

Determinism check CORRECTED: P(Response_hash | FSM_state, session, step) = 1.0 for both conditions. Grouping includes step to avoid V1 design incompatibility. Both conditions must have accuracy = 1.0.
Cardinality check: |R| per stratum at K=3. Non-trivial encoding expected to have ~3 unique hashes (one per state) vs trivial's ~60 (20 sessions x 3 states).
Conditional entropy check: H(S_next|URL, H_K=3) > 0.2 bits.
Data provenance: record session_id assignment, response generation, random seed, action sequences, response payloads with SHA-256 hashes.
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) H(S_next|URL, H_K=3) > 0.2 bits AND (2) BC PMI on non-trivial encoding at K=3 > 0.05 bits with Bonferroni p < 0.0125 AND (3) BC PMI on non-trivial encoding > BC PMI on trivial encoding (within 0.1 bits, i.e., non-trivial is not substantially worse) AND (4) positive control passes (|session-randomized BC PMI| < 3 * std(permuted PMI) on H>0 strata AND perm_null_std > 0) AND (5) determinism check passes (both conditions accuracy = 1.0 on state,session,step grouping) AND (6) >= 500 valid transitions per condition AND (7) cardinality check |R| < 0.8 * N per stratum — verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST for C-WEB-DYNAMICS. If non-trivial BC PMI <= 0.05 bits OR non-trivial not > trivial (diff < -0.1 bits) — verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING. If controls fail, ceiling not eliminated, or data quality insufficient — verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: Non-trivial page-content structure carries predictive information about Web state transitions. SPIDER should capture page content (titles, item lists, status text) as observation features for state prediction. The V10 identifiability concern is addressed: PMI persists without explicit state labels. This validates response-level observation as a viable substrate for state labeling on branching FSMs.
product_consequence_negative: Non-trivial page-content encoding yields no PMI beyond action-history memory. The parent's PMI was trivially constructed from state label injection. SPIDER should NOT invest in response-level observation for state prediction on this class of SPA. The locally-hosted testable path for C-WEB-DYNAMICS across ALL observation levels is closed.
estimated_cost: Low: locally-hosted Express server with 3-state branching FSM (reuse parent's server), 2 response conditions (non-trivial vs trivial encoding), 200 trajectories x 10 steps per condition, Python MI computation. No browser automation, no model calls. Estimated 2-3 hours total.
expected_information_gain: Very high: directly tests V10 identifiability concern — the central open question from the parent experiment. A positive result (PMI persists without state labels) demonstrates that page-content structure carries predictive information, advancing C-WEB-DYNAMICS. A negative result (PMI drops to zero) falsifies the parent's signal as trivially constructed, closing the locally-hosted testable path. Either outcome resolves the dominant unknown and enables a go/no-go decision on response-level observation.
